Before understanding the verb, you need a quick picture of the animal it comes from. A peacock is a large, beautiful bird. The male peacock has an extraordinary tail — a giant fan of feathers covered in brilliant blues, greens, and golds, each one marked with a striking eye-shaped pattern. When a male wants to attract a female, he spreads this tail wide open and struts around slowly and proudly, making sure everyone notices him.

That image — the deliberate, showy, look-at-me display — is the entire soul of the verb.

To peacock means to show yourself off in a deliberately flashy, proud, and attention-seeking way — to act, dress, or behave so that others cannot help but notice you.

It is not accidental attention. It is performed attention. The person who is peacocking knows they are doing it. They want to be looked at, admired, or talked about, and they are actively working to make that happen — just like the male bird putting on a calculated display.
The Feeling and Tone of the Word

This is important: "to peacock" almost always carries a tone of mild mockery or gentle criticism. When you say someone is peacocking, you are suggesting that their display is a little excessive, a little vain, and perhaps even slightly ridiculous — even if it is also impressive. You are not simply saying they look good. You are saying they are trying too hard to look good, or that they are far too pleased with themselves.

Think of it on a scale:

  • "He dressed nicely for the party." → neutral, no judgment
  • "He peacocked at the party." → he dressed flashily and strutted around making sure everyone saw him, and it was a bit much

The word has a smirk built into it.
How It Is Used in Real Life

Showing off appearance:
Peacocking very commonly refers to clothing and physical presentation. Someone peacocking might wear an outrageous outfit, an eye-catching accessory, or unusually bold colours — not because they simply like it, but specifically to be noticed and stand out from the crowd.

"He walked into the room peacocking in a bright red suit and a gold chain."

Showing off behaviour or status:
It is not limited to clothes. Someone can peacock by boasting loudly, walking with an exaggerated swagger, or putting their achievements on display in a way that screams look how great I am.

"After his promotion, he spent the whole week peacocking around the office."

In dating and attraction:
This is one of the most common modern uses. People often peacock to attract romantic attention — dressing boldly, acting confidently (or over-confidently), or performing their best qualities in front of someone they want to impress.

"He was clearly peacocking in front of her — flexing, laughing loudly, making sure she noticed him."

• To peacock — base form (He loves to peacock.)
  • Peacocking — the most common form you will see; the ongoing action (She was peacocking all evening.)
  • Peacocked — past tense (He peacocked his way through the entire event.)
  • Peacocks — third person singular (He peacocks whenever he gets the chance.)
A Specific, Narrower Use You Should Know

In the early 2000s, the word gained a very specific meaning in dating culture. Writers and communities focused on the art of attracting romantic partners used "peacocking" to describe a deliberate strategy: wearing something unusual, bold, or even bizarre — a feather boa, a strange hat, oversized jewellery — purely to stand out and spark conversations. The idea was that, like the bird's tail, the outrageous display would draw people toward you and make you memorable. This specific usage is still widely understood today, though the word's broader meaning (showing off in any showy, self-important way) is far more common in everyday speech.

In 19th century Australia, "peacocking" had a completely different, technical meaning: it referred to a land-grabbing strategy where settlers would deliberately purchase or claim only the best, most valuable strips of land — particularly those near water sources — making all the surrounding land useless to anyone else, since land without water access was worthless. By "peacocking" the best parts, they controlled everything. This meaning is now largely historical and you will rarely encounter it outside of discussions of Australian colonial history, but a truly complete understanding of the word includes it.

To peacock is to show off in a showy, self-admiring, attention-hungry way — through appearance, behaviour, or both — with the strong implication that the person is being vain and perhaps a little ridiculous about it, just like a male peacock spreading his spectacular tail feathers to demand everyone's gaze.
